prompt:
Extract the one contact record embedded in the user's note. Only its block of label–value lines is evidence. Recognise label variants and colon, equals or tab separators; line order is arbitrary. Ignore everything outside the block, including signatures. Reply with one bare JSON object containing exactly name, phone, email, company and country, each a string or JSON null. No prose, fences, questions or extra keys.

For every raw value, trim and collapse whitespace runs to one space. An absent or empty value, or any case of -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null or TBD, represents missing data. Do not guess. The only allowed fill for missing data is the country inference below.

Assign email and phone by content across the record, not by field label: an @ identifies email; a phone has at least seven digits and contains only digits, spaces and the characters + - ( ) . / after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension. Recognise extensions marked ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by digits. Name and company normally follow their labels. Swap them if the name-labelled value ends in a legal suffix listed below and the company-labelled value does not. Explicit country comes only from the country line.

Country owns its explicit value: convert the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, recognising English, Swedish and German country names and alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes without regard to case. Recognise common aliases, including UK and Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA and U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR and Czech Republic → CZ. Never override this country to agree with a phone.

Phone owns its written international calling code. After dropping tel: and the extension, test for an initial + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. For an international phone, replace initial 00 with +, remove the literal (0) and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the calling code as written. If the country line is absent, empty or a placeholder, use this calling code to fill country only when it belongs to exactly one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For a national phone, strip formatting and remove one leading trunk 0, then prefix + and the calling code of the normalised record country. If there is no country, a national phone is null. Non-null phones are E.164: + followed only by calling-code and national-significant-number digits.

Name: split Last, First on the first comma and put First before Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof, ignoring case and an optional dot. In each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve letters and diacritics without transliteration; comparison uses Unicode NFC.

Company: remove one trailing legal suffix, case-insensitively, along with an optional preceding comma. The suffix list for both swapping and stripping is AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.

Email: remove the mailto: prefix and enclosing angle brackets wherever they wrap the address, then lowercase it. Do not use domains, legal suffixes or surrounding text to infer or alter fields beyond the explicit rules above.
